quick: 5 mcg/kg/day SC or IV for chemo-induced neutropenia
Use only if clearly needed; no clear human risk signal
Likely compatible; minimal oral absorption by infant
CBC with differential and platelets twice weekly
summary: Filgrastim is a recombinant human G-CSF that stimulates neutrophil production. It is used to reduce febrile neutropenia in non-myeloid cancers on myelosuppressive chemotherapy, speed neutrophil recovery in AML and after bone marrow transplant, mobilize peripheral blood progenitor cells, manage severe chronic neutropenia, and treat acute radiation syndrome. Usual dose is 5 mcg/kg/day SC or IV. Key risks include splenic rupture, ARDS, serious allergic reactions and capillary leak syndrome.
indications: Reduce incidence of infection (febrile neutropenia) in non-myeloid malignancies receiving myelosuppressive chemotherapy
Reduce time to neutrophil recovery and duration of fever after induction/consolidation chemotherapy for AML
Reduce neutropenia and sequelae after myeloablative chemotherapy followed by bone marrow transplantation
Mobilize autologous hematopoietic progenitor cells for leukapheresis collection
Reduce severe neutropenia sequelae in congenital, cyclic or idiopathic neutropenia
Increase survival in patients acutely exposed to myelosuppressive doses of radiation (Hematopoietic Syndrome of Acute Radiation Syndrome)

dosage.d: 5 mcg/kg/day SC, short IV infusion (15-30 min), or continuous IV
dosage.n: Start at least 24 h after chemo; continue past expected nadir

dosage.d: 10 mcg/kg/day IV infusion over no longer than 24 hours

dosage.n: Begin >=4 days before first leukapheresis; continue until last
Start as soon as possible after exposure

admin: Give by subcutaneous injection or intravenous infusion as indicated
Do not give within 24 hours before or after cytotoxic chemotherapy
Allow refrigerated product to reach room temperature before injection; avoid shaking
Do not freeze; protect from light
moa: Filgrastim is a recombinant methionyl human granulocyte colony-stimulating factor. It binds specific G-CSF receptors on hematopoietic cells, stimulating proliferation, differentiation and end-cell functional activation of the neutrophil lineage. This increases circulating neutrophil counts and enhances neutrophil phagocytic and antibody-dependent killing functions, with minimal effect on other cell lineages.

absolute: History of serious allergic reaction to filgrastim or pegfilgrastim products
relative: Sickle cell disease (risk of sickle cell crisis)
Concurrent use with chemotherapy/radiotherapy in some solid tumors (MDS/AML signal)

preg: Available data have not established an association with major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse outcomes. Transplacental passage has been reported. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: Filgrastim is a glycoprotein and is unlikely to be absorbed by a breastfed infant; it is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding. Decide based on maternal need.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is required for renal impairment. Glomerulonephritis has been reported - consider dose reduction or interruption if it occurs.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is required for hepatic impairment. Transient elevations in alkaline phosphatase and LDH can occur.

major: Cytotoxic chemotherapy - do not give within 24 h before/after; rapidly dividing myeloid cells are sensitive to chemo
moderate: Other myeloid growth factors - avoid duplication
interactions.food: No food interaction; administered by injection.
interactions.diagnostics: Causes leukocytosis; transiently increases alkaline phosphatase, LDH and uric acid; bone-imaging uptake may increase due to marrow expansion.

monitoring: Complete blood count with differential and platelets (commonly twice weekly)
Spleen size; investigate left upper-quadrant or shoulder-tip pain
Signs of allergic reaction or fluid shifts during infusion
counsel: Bone pain is common and usually responds to simple analgesics
Report severe left upper abdominal or left shoulder pain (possible splenic problem)
Seek urgent help for breathlessness, facial swelling, rash or fainting
Store in the refrigerator, protect from light, do not freeze or shake
Keep appointments for blood count checks
pk: Neutrophil count rises within hours to days of dosing
Counts fall toward baseline within days of stopping
Refrigerate at 2-8 C (36-46 F), protect from light; do not freeze
pearls: Do not administer within 24 hours of cytotoxic chemotherapy
Bone pain is the most common adverse effect - manage with non-opioid then opioid analgesics
Evaluate left upper-quadrant or shoulder pain for splenic rupture
Avoid in sickle cell disease unless benefit outweighs crisis risk
Filgrastim and tbo-filgrastim/biosimilars share the same G-CSF mechanism
missed: If a scheduled dose is missed, contact the prescriber for timing guidance; do not double dose. Maintaining the daily schedule relative to the chemotherapy cycle is important for neutrophil recovery.
overdose: No maximum tolerated dose has been established; doses far above 10 mcg/kg/day have not produced added benefit. Marked leukocytosis (WBC >100,000) has occurred without clear adverse clinical effects. Manage by withholding the drug and monitoring blood counts.
